name: Uptime

spine.record: Immutable scheduled slot observations and explained private alert outbox

description: Private uptime console for scheduled HTTP(S), keyword, and heartbeat probes, with Base owner sign-in, installation-wide incident notifications, and portable product archives.

capabilities.description: Run signed HTTP(S), keyword, and heartbeat checks with immutable observations and explicit Unknown state.
Export and restore versioned product archives with paused definitions, portable notification definitions and histories, and preserved original state.
Send scheduled incident email, signed JSON, and Slack notifications to installation-wide destinations.

nonGoals: Real provider or production target actions before explicit authority and verification
Public communication, people paging, and independent geographic monitoring
Fresh-account hosted operation and recipient acceptance remain unverified

externals.why: An owner-directed deployment sends the application, migrations, configured Worker bindings and secrets, resource settings, and health requests to the owner's Cloudflare account; Cloudflare hosts the Worker, D1 database, and scheduled Cron.
data: Cloudflare API account and resource identities, deployment-token authorization, the Worker program and static assets, D1 schema and migrations, Cron settings, bindings, and configured deployment secret values
Deployment readiness requests and responses for the hosted Worker

Hosted Worker requests and responses carrying monitor definitions and target URLs, observations, owner identities and sessions, authentication mail state, notification events and delivery state, runner contact, and audit records
Product and installation records stored in the owner's Cloudflare D1 database, scheduled execution metadata, and configured secret bindings

externals.why: SendGrid sends hosted sign-in, incident email and monitoring watch mail when selected as the Base mail adapter.
data: SendGrid API-key authorization, sender and recipient/operator email addresses, message subject and text/HTML body, and single-use sign-in links
Delivery ID in the rer_delivery_id custom argument; click, open and analytics tracking are disabled in the submitted provider settings
Incident/test title, target URL, state, monitor and incident identity when present, probe names/outcomes/reasons, explanation, observation time, and private console URL as rendered in message content
For an owner-run drill, the one-time recipient confirmation link and drill time
Owner stale-runner identity/network-label notice or all-healthy digest text, including any monitoring-configuration warning

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a default signed JSON or custom-template webhook destination
externals.why: Owner-configured webhook (custom-webhook) sends to custom destination owner-configured-json-receiver: deliver scheduled incident events to the owner's public HTTPS endpoint. The endpoint runs outside this installation.
data: The configured public HTTPS endpoint receives the selected GET, POST, PUT or PATCH request with JSON, form or query parameters, configured local custom header values, optional signature/timestamp headers, source address and delivery time
Event ID, type, incident key, monitor ID and revision, name, target URL, scheduled slot, state, observation time, probe outcomes and reasons, explanation, and private console URL

Versioned custom templates may send the documented monitor, incident, location, timing, certificate/domain expiry and heartbeat facts, including owner-zone times. Custom header values and signing keys stay encrypted locally and are excluded from lists and archives. Only an explicit owner request preview shows the receiver URL; its header secrets and signatures are masked.
A drill event additionally carries the one-time recipient confirmation URL, start time, and expiry; ordinary incident and test events do not
The endpoint's bounded HTTP status, headers and response body return to the dispatcher; the owner sees status and an escaped, secret-scrubbed excerpt of at most 512 characters

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a Slack incoming-webhook destination
externals.why: Slack (slack) sends to provider destination slack-incoming-webhook: post escaped notification content to the owner's incoming webhook. Slack runs outside this installation and accepts the configured remote request.
data: The configured Slack webhook receives the escaped message body, source address, and delivery time
Incident title and state, monitor identity and target URL, probe outcomes and reasons, explanation, observation time, and console URL
A drill message additionally carries the one-time recipient confirmation URL and drill time
The endpoint's bounded HTTP status, headers, and response body return to the runner for delivery classification

externals.why: Owner-selected independent HTTPS heartbeat service; optional empty GET while self-check passes. The configured URL is a capability and its path is sent to that service.
data: HTTPS host and capability path from the owner-configured URL, request time, and source network address; no request body or product record
The heartbeat service's response status is read and its response body is canceled rather than retained

externals.why: Independent webhook or Slack notice configured only in the runner environment.
data: Owner-configured webhook receives only unreachable/restored state and times; owner-configured Slack receives the same short notice text
Notification URL capability, runner source address, and request time; no monitor name, target URL, probe result, or product event
The destination's bounded status, response headers, and response body are read for transport classification

externals.requiredWhen: The shared local lifecycle checks a selected application origin before starting its runner
externals.why: The local setup/dev/preview lifecycle checks the selected Uptime application readiness endpoint; it may be local loopback or an owner-selected remote origin.
data: A GET request for the selected application's readiness URL and any HTTP redirect destinations followed by the CLI; no request body or configured authorization header is sent
The destination sees the CLI source address and request timing; the CLI reads only the returned health status and JSON readiness value

externals.requiredWhen: A target, discovery page, flow subresource, notification endpoint, heartbeat, runner control plane, or configured provider hostname needs DNS resolution
externals.why: Private runners and owner tools use their configured DNS resolver. Hosted public checks validate A/AAAA answers through Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS; Workers fetch uses Cloudflare’s public Internet resolver and transport.
data: Queried hostnames for A/AAAA or system address lookup, resolver source address, and lookup timing; DNS carries no URL path, request body, or HTTP credential
Hosted checks send the target and canary hostnames as A/AAAA queries to https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query; no target URL path, body or credential is included.

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a public HTTP(S) monitor, assigns an external canary, or authorizes an OAuth HTTPS token endpoint in a monitor-bound runner credential file
externals.why: The hosted Worker or an explicitly assigned private runner sends scheduled requests to the owner’s public target and optional canary URLs. A private runner also acquires or refreshes OAuth tokens only at the exact public HTTPS token URL authorized in that monitor's local credential file.
data: Target hostname, path and query, method, request time and runner source address; configured headers and request body where the monitor has them

Owner-held Basic, bearer or Digest credentials, generated JWT authorization and configured headers/body are sent only to the exact authorized target origin and monitor; a configured client TLS certificate and proof of key possession may be sent there, while its private key remains local. Credentials, custom headers, body and client certificate are permanently stripped on a cross-origin redirect

Owner-authorized OAuth token acquisition and refresh send a form-encoded HTTPS POST to the exact public token URL: client ID and secret through the declared Basic or form authentication mode, grant type, requested scopes and the refresh token when applicable. Public DNS answers are validated and pinned; token redirects and target TLS trust exceptions are refused. Acquired access and rotated refresh tokens remain in owner-only runner-local state, outside observations, logs and product archives
The target returns status and headers plus a bounded response body used for assertions; raw response bodies are not retained in observations
An external canary is a status-only GET: it sends no request credential, custom header or body and reads zero response-body bytes; validated public redirect hops may also be contacted

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a TCP or TLS monitor
externals.why: The hosted Worker or an assigned private runner opens a connection to the owner's public host and port to check that it accepts connections, its banner or its certificate.
data: Target host name, port, the validated public address connected to, connection time and the vantage's source address
A TCP check sends no data; with banner reading on, it reads at most 512 bytes the service sends first and keeps at most 256 printable characters

A TLS check sends a TLS ClientHello naming the host (SNI); the Worker reads the certificate chain from a TLS 1.2 handshake it does not complete and then makes one verified connection without sending application data; certificate subject, issuer, names, validity and SHA-256 fingerprint are retained
Private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses are refused before connecting; the Worker also refuses Cloudflare addresses, which its sockets cannot reach, and reports that vantage Unknown

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a DNS monitor, or the Worker validates a TCP, TLS or registry host
externals.why: DNS monitors ask the owner-selected public resolvers (Cloudflare at cloudflare-dns.com, Google at dns.google) over HTTPS; the Worker also resolves TCP, TLS and registry hosts through Cloudflare before connecting.
data: The queried name and record type, request time and the vantage's source address
The resolver returns its answer code and records; at most ten normalised records of at most 255 characters per resolver and the response time are retained

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a domain registration monitor
externals.why: Domain monitors read IANA's RDAP bootstrap (data.iana.org), the domain's registry RDAP service it names and the registrar RDAP record the registry links, over HTTPS only.
data: The monitored domain name, request time and the vantage's source address

Registry and registrar answers are read up to 64 KiB (the bootstrap up to 256 KiB); retained are each source URL and update time, the expiry date, registry status values and whether the date is redacted or the sources conflict

externals.requiredWhen: An owner asks to check a public website or configures UPTIME_START_URL
externals.why: The runner performs bounded read-only discovery of the owner's chosen site, following its public redirects and crawling permitted pages and related API/status hosts.
data: The owner-selected URL, request host/path/query, GET or HEAD method, discovery User-Agent and other headers, request time, and runner source address

The initial URL's public redirect chain, then robots files, pages, JSON/spec documents and redirect destinations on its permitted registrable domains and linked status hosts are read with bounded bodies in runner memory

Only the input/final URL, contacted hostnames, request count and duration, short notes, and validated proposed monitor definitions return to the console; raw target HTML, JSON and response headers are not returned, stored, logged, or rendered as console HTML

externals.requiredWhen: An owner enables a browser-flow monitor on a runner with a browser
externals.why: A fresh runner browser follows owner-defined flows through the filtering proxy; target pages and their public network dependencies receive ordinary browser requests.
data: Owner-defined top-level URLs and paths, redirects that remain within the declared origins, and requests to public subresources and WebSocket destinations initiated by those pages; DNS names, source address, and request timing are visible at the relevant destinations

Browser-generated request headers, referrer/origin information, and cookies a destination sets may be sent to the relevant public destination; page content is processed locally in the runner to execute steps, while no raw page body or screenshot returns in the control-plane result or observation

A named owner-held flow credential is filled only at its exact configured origin and may be sent by that site-form submission; the secret itself remains in runner-local custody and is redacted from traces

Private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses are blocked; top-level navigation is limited to declared origins, while public subresources and WebSockets are individually passed through the filtering proxy

externals.requiredWhen: A private runner is enrolled and polls the owner's configured UPTIME_CONTROL_ORIGIN
externals.why: The separately operated runner uses signed HTTPS requests to the configured Uptime Worker control plane for enrolment, claims, results, discovery, notification custody, and contact.
data: Runner key authentication and signature, runner identity, declared network label, browser capability, request times, and claimed task identifiers
Assigned monitor and flow definitions, canary URLs, retry and lease data, and signed attempt evidence, including status, assertions, timings, and bounded flow trace
Discovery input URLs and derived host/proposal results

For notification delivery, the claimed endpoint URL, signing credential and event payload are returned to the runner for the one configured send; signed outcome and bounded provider response details return to the Worker

externals.requiredWhen: Only when the owner selects an optional identity-provider address during setup; no provider sign-in is enabled by that selection
externals.why: The shared setup CLI can read selected provider discovery documents. The completed local probe read dependency metadata, then failed at unmounted application dependency approval (404) before owner creation or any provider link request. Uptime does not mount linked-provider routes; runtime OIDC callback, token, JWKS and dependency exchange are unsupported.
data: Selected issuer hostname and read-only setup requests for its OIDC configuration, RER provider document, and dependency-interface metadata

A setup approval request to the Uptime origin carries issuer/interface and the configured setup token; the current unmounted route returns 404 before owner creation. The measured probe made no one-time provider link request. A future shared linking path may send app origin, interface and a temporary link capability, requiring separate adoption and evidence.

No linked sign-in, authorization-code callback, runtime token/JWKS exchange or user-profile exchange is implemented by the current Uptime server; do not infer an operational provider integration from the optional declaration

externals.requiredWhen: Only when the owner configures the exact RER_MANAGEMENT_ORIGIN and installation ID for the private management editor
externals.why: An authenticated owner page may create the configured management editor iframe while the editor is hidden. This is an explicit private management integration, not a public embeddable widget. This is the explicit BASE-DATA-005 exception: the configured origin may belong to the author and receive opted-in requests; the native product has no operational dependency on this integration.
data: The exact configured management origin receives an iframe request containing the installation ID, parent page origin, and editor surface; after handshake it also receives the current page path

Rendered page title and up to 60 visible text/element descriptors are sent only after the owner opens the editor and explicitly enables context sharing; form values and private-marked elements are excluded
Editor protocol messages, live-edit requests and results are exchanged with the configured management origin

externals.why: Resend sends hosted sign-in, incident email and monitoring watch mail when selected as the Base mail adapter.
data: Resend API-key authorization, sender and recipient/operator email addresses, message subject and text/HTML body, and single-use sign-in links
Delivery ID in the Idempotency-Key request header
Incident/test title, target URL, state, monitor and incident identity when present, probe names/outcomes/reasons, explanation, observation time, and private console URL as rendered in message content
For an owner-run drill, the one-time recipient confirmation link and drill time
Owner stale-runner identity/network-label notice or all-healthy digest text, including any monitoring-configuration warning

externals.why: Cloudflare Email Sending sends hosted sign-in, incident email and monitoring watch mail when selected as the Base mail adapter.
data: Cloudflare API-key authorization and configured account identity, sender and recipient/operator email addresses, message subject and text/HTML body, and single-use sign-in links
Account-scoped email-sending API request with no Uptime attachment payload
Incident/test title, target URL, state, monitor and incident identity when present, probe names/outcomes/reasons, explanation, observation time, and private console URL as rendered in message content
For an owner-run drill, the one-time recipient confirmation link and drill time
Owner stale-runner identity/network-label notice or all-healthy digest text, including any monitoring-configuration warning

env.name: SENDGRID_API_KEY
env.requiredWhen: When hosted sign-in or an email notification destination is enabled
env.why: Authenticates Base mail sending through SendGrid; load it from server-side secret storage and never expose it to browser code or logs.

env.name: UPTIME_HEARTBEAT_URL
env.why: External public HTTPS heartbeat capability URL; off when absent.

env.name: UPTIME_START_URL
env.why: Website the owner chose at setup; first-run setup asks the owner's runner to look at it. Off when absent.

env.name: IDENTITY_PROVIDER
env.why: Optional setup-only identity-provider address. Omitted uses native email-link setup; selecting a provider currently fails at unmounted dependency approval before owner creation and does not enable linked OIDC sign-in.

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER_API_KEY
env.why: Resend API key selected at setup.

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_MAIL_API_KEY
env.why: Cloudflare Email Sending API key selected at setup.

env.name: MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID
env.why: Cloudflare Email Sending account selected at setup.

env.name: UPTIME_RUNNER_ID
env.why: Per-runner identity returned at enrolment or provisioning; legacy runner may omit it.

env.name: UPTIME_NETWORK_LABEL
env.why: Runner-local declared network label; must match its provisioned identity.

env.name: UPTIME_WATCH_WEBHOOK_URL
env.why: Independent HTTPS notice capability URL, kept only in the runner environment.

env.name: UPTIME_WATCH_SLACK_URL
env.why: Independent Slack notice capability URL, kept only in the runner environment.

env.name: UPTIME_WATCH_AFTER_MS
env.why: Runner-local failed-poll notice interval; defaults to three minutes.

env.name: UPTIME_WATCH_REPEAT_MS
env.why: Notice repeat interval on the runner or Worker; defaults to one hour.

env.name: UPTIME_RUNNER_STALE_MS
env.why: Worker stale-contact interval; defaults to two minutes.

env.name: UPTIME_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS
env.why: Worker external heartbeat interval; defaults to five minutes.

env.name: UPTIME_DIGEST_INTERVAL_MS
env.why: Worker healthy digest interval; defaults to one week.

deploy.notes: Console documents and APIs require a Base owner session; runner and heartbeat APIs use separately scoped credentials.

limits.notes: Owner-tunable source settings; each class shares one fixed 60-second D1 window per client. Production assets retain their own budget. Local Vite compiler assets use a separate budget for the unbundled browser graph: about 140 module requests per console load, with room for twelve loads per minute. These defaults are estimated, not load tested. Hosted CF-Connecting-IP must be a valid single IP; missing/malformed values share an unknown-client bucket. Local mode ignores all forwarding headers and uses one loopback bucket. Only keyed hashes of client identities are stored.
